chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Hammam, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who bequeathed wealth for his relatives at the time of his death, and emancipated a slave of his, and the entirety of what he bequeathed exceeded one-third. How should one deal with his bequest? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the emancipation, and enforce it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the priority of emancipating a slave when bequests exceed one-third of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the priority of 'abd al-mudabbir' (manumission) in estate distribution, establishing that freeing a slave is executed in full before other bequests are considered, even if it exceeds the standard one-third limit. This ruling highlights the high spiritual status of manumission in Shia jurisprudence, treating it as a debt to God that takes precedence over charitable gifts or bequests to relatives. The precedence reflects the principle that liberation of a soul is a more significant act of worship than material distribution.
